These provide specialized guidance for the current task. Use this when you identify a task that matches a skill's description. ONLY use names exactly as they appear in the `<available_skills>` section.

functionDeclarations.name: analyze_multimedia
functionDeclarations.description:
Analyzes images, videos, and audio files using a multimodal model. This tool accepts local file paths, base64 data, or URLs to multimedia content. Supported formats include common image types (PNG, JPG, GIF, WEBP, BMP), video formats (MP4, MKV, OGG), and audio formats (MP3, WAV, FLAC, OGG, M4A).

Key capabilities:
• Visual Agent: Operates PC/mobile GUIs, recognizes UI elements, understands functions, can guide through interface interactions
• Visual Coding: Generates Draw.io diagrams, HTML/CSS/JS code from images/videos
• Text Extraction: Reads and extracts all text from images including documents, receipts, screenshots
• Spatial Perception: Judges object positions, viewpoints, occlusions, provides 2D grounding
• Content Analysis: Describes scenes, identifies objects, analyzes actions in videos
• Audio Understanding: Transcribes speech, identifies sounds, analyzes audio content
• Technical Understanding: Interprets charts, diagrams, technical drawings, code screenshots

The model responds based on your specific prompt. Examples: 'Extract all text from this receipt', 'Generate HTML code for this UI design', 'Identify all clickable elements in this screenshot', 'Describe the spatial relationships between objects', 'Transcribe the speech in this audio', 'What sounds are in this recording?'.

content.description: The multimedia content. For 'absolute_path': provide the absolute file path. For 'base64': provide base64 data (with or without 'data:mime/type;base64,' prefix). For 'url': provide the complete URL starting with http:// or https://.

prompt.description: The prompt or question to ask about the multimedia content. Be specific about what you want to know. Examples: 'Describe what you see in this image', 'Extract all text from this receipt', 'Generate HTML/CSS code for this UI design', 'Identify all clickable elements and their functions in this screenshot', 'What actions are happening in this video?', 'Create a Draw.io diagram based on this flowchart image', 'Describe the spatial relationships between objects', 'What UI components are visible and how can I interact with them?', 'Transcribe the speech in this audio file', 'What sounds can you hear in this recording?', 'Identify the speakers in this conversation'.

type.description: Question type: 'choice' (default) for multiple-choice with options, 'text' for free-form input, 'yesno' for Yes/No confirmation.

options.description: Selectable choices for 'choice' type questions. Provide 2-4 options.

functionDeclarations.name: glob
functionDeclarations.description: Efficiently finds files matching specific glob patterns (e.g., `src/**/*.ts`, `**/*.md`), returning absolute paths sorted by modification time (newest first). Ideal for quickly locating files based on their name or path structure, especially in large codebases.

functionDeclarations.name: job_create
functionDeclarations.description:
Use this tool to create a structured task list for your current coding session. This helps you track progress, organize complex tasks, and demonstrate thoroughness to the user.
It also helps the user understand the progress of the job and overall progress of their requests.

## When to Use This Tool
Use this tool proactively in these scenarios:
- Complex multi-step tasks - When a job requires 3 or more distinct steps or actions
- Non-trivial and complex tasks - Work that requires careful planning or multiple operations
- Plan mode - When using plan mode, create a job list to track the work
- User explicitly requests job list - When the user directly asks you to use the job list
- User provides multiple tasks - When users provide a list of things to be done (numbered or comma-separated)
- After receiving new instructions - Immediately capture user requirements as jobs
- When you start working on a job - Mark it as in_progress BEFORE beginning work
- After completing a job - Mark it as completed and add any new follow-up jobs discovered during implementation

## When NOT to Use This Tool
Skip using this tool when:
- There is only a single, straightforward job
- The job is trivial and tracking it provides no organizational benefit
- The job can be completed in less than 3 trivial steps
- The job is purely conversational or informational

NOTE that you should not use this tool if there is only one trivial job to do. In this case you are better off just doing the job directly.

## Job Fields
- **subject**: A brief, actionable title in imperative form (e.g., "Fix authentication bug in login flow")
- **description**: Detailed description of what needs to be done, including context and acceptance criteria
- **activeForm**: Present continuous form shown in spinner when job is in_progress (e.g., "Fixing authentication bug"). This is displayed to the user while you work on the job.

**IMPORTANT**: Always provide activeForm when creating jobs. The subject should be imperative ("Run tests") while activeForm should be present continuous ("Running tests"). All jobs are created with status `pending`.

## Tips
- Create jobs with clear, specific subjects that describe the outcome
- Include enough detail in the description for another agent to understand and complete the job
- After creating jobs, use job_update to set up dependencies (blocks/blockedBy) if needed
- Check job_list first to avoid creating duplicate jobs
- Use `allowDuplicate: true` only when you intentionally need a second open job with the same normalized subject

subject.description: A brief title for the job

description.description: A detailed description of what needs to be done

activeForm.description: Present continuous form shown in spinner when in_progress (e.g., "Running tests")

metadata.description: Arbitrary metadata to attach to the job

allowDuplicate.description: Set to true to force creation even if a duplicate open job already exists

functionDeclarations.name: job_get
functionDeclarations.description:
Use this tool to retrieve a job by its ID from the job list.

## When to Use This Tool
- When you need the full description and context before starting work on a job
- To understand job dependencies (what it blocks, what blocks it)
- After being assigned a job, to get complete requirements

## Output
Returns full job details:
- **subject**: Job title
- **description**: Detailed requirements and context
- **status**: 'pending', 'in_progress', 'failed', or 'completed'
- **blocks**: Jobs waiting on this one to complete
- **blockedBy**: Jobs that must complete before this one can start

## Tips
- After fetching a job, verify its blockedBy list is empty before beginning work.
- Use job_list to see all jobs in summary form.

jobId.description: The ID of the job to retrieve

functionDeclarations.name: job_list
functionDeclarations.description:
Use this tool to list all jobs in the job list.

## When to Use This Tool
- To see what jobs are available to work on (status: 'pending', no owner, not blocked)
- To check overall progress on the project
- To find jobs that are blocked and need dependencies resolved
- After completing a job, to check for newly unblocked work or claim the next available job
- **Prefer working on jobs in ID order** (lowest ID first) when multiple jobs are available, as earlier jobs often set up context for later ones

## Continuation Workflow

- After completing your current job, call job_list to find available work
- Look first for jobs with status 'pending', no owner, and empty blockedBy
- If multiple jobs are available, prefer the lowest-ID job first
- If no jobs are available, remaining work is either completed or blocked and should be handled explicitly

## Output
Returns a summary of each job:
- **id**: Job identifier (use with job_get, job_update)
- **subject**: Brief description of the job
- **status**: 'pending', 'in_progress', 'failed', or 'completed'
- **owner**: Current execution owner identifier if assigned (auto-linked task execution uses task IDs like `task-1`), empty if available
- **blockedBy**: List of open job IDs that must be resolved first (jobs with blockedBy cannot be claimed until dependencies resolve)

Use job_get with a specific job ID to view full details including description and comments.

functionDeclarations.name: job_update
functionDeclarations.description:
Use this tool to update a job in the job list.

## When to Use This Tool
**Mark jobs as resolved:**
- When you have completed the work described in a job
- When a job is no longer needed or has been superseded
- IMPORTANT: Always mark your assigned jobs as resolved when you finish them
- After resolving, call job_list to find your next job
- After completing your current job, look for the next available job instead of stopping
- Available jobs are typically: status = 'pending', no owner, and no open blockedBy dependencies
- **Prefer working on jobs in ID order** (lowest ID first) when multiple jobs are available, as earlier jobs often set up context for later ones
- ONLY mark a job as completed when you have FULLY accomplished it
- If you encounter errors, blockers, or cannot finish, keep the job as in_progress
- When blocked, create a new job describing what needs to be resolved
- Never mark a job as completed if:
  - Tests are failing
  - Implementation is partial
  - You encountered unresolved errors
  - You couldn't find necessary files or dependencies

**Delete jobs:**
- When a job is no longer relevant or was created in error
- Setting status to `deleted` permanently removes the job

**Update job details:**
- When requirements change or become clearer
- When establishing dependencies between jobs

## Fields You Can Update
- **status**: The job status (see Status Workflow below)
- **subject**: Change the job title (imperative form, e.g., "Run tests")
- **description**: Change the job description
- **activeForm**: Present continuous form shown in spinner when in_progress (e.g., "Running tests")
- **owner**: Change the job owner identifier. When a job is auto-linked to a `task`, this is typically the execution task ID (e.g. `task-1`).
- **metadata**: Merge metadata keys into the job (set a key to null to delete it)
- **addBlocks**: Mark jobs that cannot start until this one completes
- **addBlockedBy**: Mark jobs that must complete before this one can start
- **removeBlocks**: Remove jobs from this job's blocks list
- **removeBlockedBy**: Remove jobs from this job's blocked-by list

## Status Workflow
Status progresses: `pending` → `in_progress` → `completed`
A job can also move to `failed` when a linked task fails, then back to `in_progress` for retry.
Use `deleted` to permanently remove a job.

## Staleness
Make sure to read a job's latest state using `job_get` before updating it.

## Continuation

- After marking a job completed, use `job_list` to check for newly unblocked work
- If a clear unblocked job exists, continue with it rather than pausing for an unnecessary decision
- If no job is available, or remaining work is genuinely blocked or ambiguous, then ask the user or update dependencies accordingly

## Examples
Mark job as in progress when starting work:
```json
{"jobId": "1", "status": "in_progress"}
```
Mark job as completed after finishing work:
```json
{"jobId": "1", "status": "completed"}
```
Delete a job:
```json
{"jobId": "1", "status": "deleted"}
```
Claim a job by setting owner:
```json
{"jobId": "1", "owner": "task-1"}
```
Set up job dependencies:
```json
{"jobId": "2", "addBlockedBy": ["1"]}
```
Remove a dependency after recovering:
```json
{"jobId": "2", "removeBlockedBy": ["1"]}
```

jobId.description: The ID of the job to update

activeForm.description: Present continuous form shown in spinner when in_progress (e.g., "Running tests")

addBlocks.description: Job IDs that this job blocks

addBlockedBy.description: Job IDs that block this job

removeBlocks.description: Job IDs to remove from this job's blocks list

removeBlockedBy.description: Job IDs to remove from this job's blocked-by list

metadata.description: Metadata keys to merge into the job. Set a key to null to delete it.

functionDeclarations.name: list_directory
functionDeclarations.description: Lists the names of files and subdirectories directly within a specified directory path. Can optionally ignore entries matching provided glob patterns.

path.description: The absolute path to the directory to list (must be absolute, not relative)

ignore.description: List of glob patterns to ignore

file_filtering_options.description: Optional: Whether to respect ignore patterns from .gitignore or .geminiignore

respect_git_ignore.description: Optional: Whether to respect .gitignore patterns when listing files. Only available in git repositories. Defaults to true.

respect_gemini_ignore.description: Optional: Whether to respect .geminiignore patterns when listing files. Defaults to true.

functionDeclarations.name: lsp
functionDeclarations.description: Interact with LSP servers for code intelligence: definition, references, hover, symbols, implementation, and call hierarchy.

filePath.description: Absolute or relative file path in workspace.

functionDeclarations.name: read_file
functionDeclarations.description: Reads and returns the content of a specified file. By default reads up to 2000 lines starting from the beginning of the file. Files whose selected range exceeds 256 KB are truncated with an advisory; use 'offset' and 'limit' only if the file is too large to read at once — it's recommended to read the whole file by not providing these parameters. Handles text, images (PNG, JPG, GIF, WEBP, SVG, BMP), and PDF files. For images, videos or other multimedia files, use the 'analyze_multimedia' tool if available.

absolute_path.description: The absolute path to the file to read (e.g., '/home/user/project/file.txt'). Relative paths are not supported. You must provide an absolute path.

offset.description: Optional: For text files, the 0-based line number to start reading from. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once.

limit.description: Optional: For text files, the maximum number of lines to read. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once.

functionDeclarations.name: read_many_files
functionDeclarations.description:
Reads content from multiple files specified by paths or glob patterns within a configured target directory. For text files, it concatenates their content into a single string. It is primarily designed for text-based files. However, it can also process image (e.g., .png, .jpg) and PDF (.pdf) files if their file names or extensions are explicitly included in the 'paths' argument. For these explicitly requested non-text files, their data is read and included in a format suitable for model consumption (e.g., base64 encoded).

This tool is useful when you need to understand or analyze a collection of files, such as:
- Getting an overview of a codebase or parts of it (e.g., all TypeScript files in the 'src' directory).
- Finding where specific functionality is implemented if the user asks broad questions about code.
- Reviewing documentation files (e.g., all Markdown files in the 'docs' directory).
- Gathering context from multiple configuration files.
- When the user asks to "read all files in X directory" or "show me the content of all Y files".

Use this tool when the user's query implies needing the content of several files simultaneously for context, analysis, or summarization. For text files, it uses default UTF-8 encoding and a '--- {filePath} ---' separator between file contents. Ensure paths are relative to the target directory. Glob patterns like 'src/**/*.js' are supported. Avoid using for single files if a more specific single-file reading tool is available, unless the user specifically requests to process a list containing just one file via this tool. Other binary files (not explicitly requested as image/PDF) are generally skipped. Default excludes apply to common non-text files (except for explicitly requested images/PDFs) and large dependency directories unless 'useDefaultExcludes' is false.

paths.description: Required. An array of glob patterns or paths relative to the tool's target directory. Examples: ['src/**/*.ts'], ['README.md', 'docs/']

include.description: Optional. Additional glob patterns to include. These are merged with `paths`. Example: "*.test.ts" to specifically add test files if they were broadly excluded.

exclude.description: Optional. Glob patterns for files/directories to exclude. Added to default excludes if useDefaultExcludes is true. Example: "**/*.log", "temp/"

recursive.description: Optional. Whether to search recursively (primarily controlled by `**` in glob patterns). Defaults to true.

useDefaultExcludes.description: Optional. Whether to apply a list of default exclusion patterns (e.g., node_modules, .git, binary files). Defaults to true.

file_filtering_options.description: Whether to respect ignore patterns from .gitignore or .geminiignore

respect_git_ignore.description: Optional: Whether to respect .gitignore patterns when listing files. Only available in git repositories. Defaults to true.

respect_gemini_ignore.description: Optional: Whether to respect .geminiignore patterns when listing files. Defaults to true.

functionDeclarations.name: replace
functionDeclarations.description:
Replaces text within a file. Use this tool for targeted edits to existing files.

The tool replaces exactly ONE occurrence of `old_string` with `new_string` by default. The `old_string` MUST uniquely identify the specific instance to change — unless `replace_all` is set to true, in which case every occurrence of `old_string` will be replaced. Use the read_file tool to establish the current file state before the first text replacement. If the tool reports that the file changed since it was read, re-read it before retrying.

If you need to replace the full contents of an existing file, use `write_file` instead.
If `old_string` is empty, the tool treats the operation as creating a new file. This is only valid when the target file does not already exist.
Do not use an empty `old_string` to overwrite an existing file.

The user has the ability to modify the `new_string` content. If modified, this will be stated in the response.

Expectation for required parameters:
1. `file_path` MUST be an absolute path; otherwise an error will be thrown.
2. Prefer exact literal text for `old_string`, including relevant surrounding context and matching whitespace, indentation, and newlines when possible.
3. Prefer exact literal text for `new_string`, and ensure the resulting code is correct and idiomatic.
4. NEVER escape `old_string` or `new_string`, that would break the exact literal text requirement.

**Important:** Exact literal matches are the most reliable. The tool may also apply limited deterministic normalization for whitespace, indentation, and escaping, but do not rely on fallback matching when you can provide the exact text. The edit will FAIL if `old_string` is not unique in the file. Either provide a larger string with more surrounding context to make it unique or use `replace_all` to change every instance of `old_string`.
Use `replace_all` for replacing and renaming strings across the file. This parameter is useful if you want to rename a variable for instance.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to modify. Must start with '/'.

old_string.description: Prefer exact literal text when possible, preferably unescaped. Include at least 3 lines of context BEFORE and AFTER the target text, matching whitespace and indentation as closely as you can. The `old_string` should uniquely match one location in the file unless `replace_all` is true. Exact matches are the most reliable, and the tool may also apply limited deterministic normalization for whitespace, indentation, and escaping when needed. If `old_string` is empty, the tool treats the operation as creating a new file. This is only valid when the target file does not already exist.

new_string.description: Prefer exact literal text to replace `old_string` with, preferably unescaped. Provide the intended final text and ensure the resulting code is correct and idiomatic.

replace_all.description: Replace all occurrences of old_string (default false). Use this for replacing and renaming strings across the file.

functionDeclarations.name: run_shell_command
functionDeclarations.description:
This tool executes a given shell command using the best available Windows shell (PowerShell Core, Windows PowerShell, or Command Prompt).

IMPORTANT:
- This tool is for terminal operations (e.g., git / npm / docker / build & test commands).
- DO NOT use this tool for file operations like reading, writing, editing, or searching files. Prefer the dedicated file tools for those actions.
- Quote any file path that contains spaces with double quotes, e.g. `cd "/path with spaces"` or `python "/path with spaces/script.py"`.
- If a command would produce very large output, prefer adding flags/filters (narrow paths, limit counts, request specific fields, machine-readable formats like JSON) to keep output small and unambiguous.
- Very large outputs may be returned as the most recent tail of the output. Earlier content may be truncated from the beginning. If the tool reports a "Full output saved to: <path>", that file contains the full command output. Use the exact path returned by the tool, then prefer searching that file first (grep/rg or platform equivalents) for specific ERROR/WARN/FAIL/SUCCESS markers, then reading small slices (with `read_file` using `offset`/`limit`) or tailing the log file instead of re-running expensive commands.
- Do not append truncating pipelines such as `| tail`, `| Select-Object -Last`, or similar to an expensive first run just to suppress output. Those discard earlier context and force a re-run if you later need omitted lines. Let the tool/log capture the full output, then inspect the saved log file.
- When issuing multiple shell commands in one response, parallelize only when they are truly independent and do not compete for the same files, directories, logs, locks, caches, git state, or ports. If one command depends on another or shared state may race, run them sequentially.

The following information is returned:
- Command: Executed command.
- Directory: Directory where command was executed, or `(root)`.
- Output: Combined command output (stdout/stderr). Can be `(empty)` or an excerpt if very large.
- Error: Error or `(none)` if no error was reported for the subprocess.
- Exit Code: Exit code or `(none)` if terminated by signal.
- Signal: Signal number or `(none)` if no signal was received.

command.description: Exact command to execute using the best available Windows shell (automatically selected from PowerShell Core, Windows PowerShell, or Command Prompt). Quote any file paths containing spaces with double quotes.

description.description: Brief description of the command for the user. Be specific and concise. Ideally a single sentence. Can be up to 3 sentences for clarity. No line breaks.

directory.description: (OPTIONAL) The absolute path of the directory to run the command in. If not provided, the project root directory is used. Must be a directory within the workspace and must already exist.

run_in_background.description: Set to true to run this command in the background. Returns immediately with task metadata and an output file path.

functionDeclarations.name: save_memory
functionDeclarations.description:
Saves a specific piece of information or fact to your long-term memory.

Use this tool:

- When the user explicitly asks you to remember something (e.g., "Remember that I like pineapple on pizza", "Please save this: my cat's name is Whiskers").
- When the user states a clear, concise fact about themselves, their preferences, or their environment that seems important for you to retain for future interactions to provide a more personalized and effective assistance.

Do NOT use this tool:

- To remember conversational context that is only relevant for the current session.
- To save long, complex, or rambling pieces of text. The fact should be relatively short and to the point.
- If you are unsure whether the information is a fact worth remembering long-term. If in doubt, you can ask the user, "Should I remember that for you?"

## Parameters

- `fact` (string, required): The specific fact or piece of information to remember. This should be a clear, self-contained statement. For example, if the user says "My favorite color is blue", the fact would be "My favorite color is blue".
- `scope` (string, optional): Where to save the memory:
  - "global": Saves to user-level ~/.codely-cli/CODELY.md (shared across all projects)
  - "project": Saves to current project's CODELY.md (project-specific)
  - If not specified, the tool will ask the user where they want to save the memory.

fact.description: The specific fact or piece of information to remember. Should be a clear, self-contained statement.

scope.description: Where to save the memory: "global" saves to user-level ~/.codely-cli/CODELY.md (shared across all projects), "project" saves to current project's CODELY.md (project-specific). If not specified, will prompt user to choose.

functionDeclarations.name: search_file_content
functionDeclarations.description: Searches for a regular expression pattern within the content of files in a specified directory, a specific file, or the current working directory. Can filter files by a glob pattern when searching directories. Returns the lines containing matches, along with their file paths and line numbers.

pattern.description: The regular expression (regex) pattern to search for within file contents (e.g., 'function\s+myFunction', 'import\s+\{.*\}\s+from\s+.*').

path.description: Optional: The absolute path to a directory or file to search within. If a file path is provided, searches only within that file. If a directory path is provided, searches all files in that directory. If omitted, searches the current working directory.

include.description: Optional: A glob pattern to filter which files are searched (e.g., '*.js', '*.{ts,tsx}', 'src/**'). Only applicable when searching directories, ignored for file searches. If omitted, searches all files (respecting potential global ignores).

maxResults.description: Optional: Maximum number of matches to return to prevent context overflow (default: 20, max: 150). Values above 150 are clamped automatically. Use lower values for broad searches, higher for specific searches.

functionDeclarations.name: task
functionDeclarations.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks autonomously.

The Task tool launches specialized agents that autonomously handle complex tasks. Each agent has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agents (use these names as the subagent_name value):
- explore: Fast read-only codebase search agent for finding files, patterns, and answering questions about the codebase. Use when you need to quickly find files by patterns, search code for keywords, or understand how parts of the codebase work. Specify thoroughness: 'quick' for basic searches, 'medium' for moderate exploration, 'very thorough' for comprehensive analysis. (Tools: All tools except replace, write_file, apply_patch, save_memory)
- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)
- plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except replace, write_file, apply_patch, save_memory)

Agent selection guidance:
- For codebase search, file discovery, or answering "where is X" questions, prefer the explore agent instead of general-purpose — it is faster and read-only.
- Use explore for quick searches, code pattern discovery, and understanding how parts of the codebase work.
- Use the plan agent for designing implementation strategies before writing code — it explores the codebase and returns a step-by-step plan with critical files.
- Prefer plan over general-purpose when the user asks to design, architect, or plan before implementing.
- Use general-purpose for multi-step tasks that require writing code, running commands, or performing actions beyond read-only exploration.

When using the Task tool, you must set the subagent_name parameter to one of the agent names listed above (e.g., "general-purpose").

When NOT to use the Task tool:
- If you want to read a specific file path, use the read_file or glob tool instead of the Task tool, to find the match more quickly
- If you are searching for a specific class definition like "class Foo", use the glob tool instead, to find the match more quickly
- If you are searching for code within a specific file or set of 2-3 files, use the read_file tool instead of the Task tool, to find the match more quickly
- Other tasks that are not related to the agent descriptions above

Usage notes:
- Always include a short description (3-5 words) summarizing what the agent will do
- Launch multiple agents concurrently whenever possible, to maximize performance; to do that, use a single message with multiple tool uses
- When the agent is done, it will return a single message back to you. The result returned by the agent is not visible to the user. To show the user the result, you should send a text message back to the user with a concise summary of the result.
- Optional display name: the name parameter is only for UI/tracking display. If omitted, description is used as the display name.
- You can optionally run agents in the background using the run_in_background parameter, but only for genuinely independent work. When an agent runs in the background, you will be notified when it completes.
- Foreground is the default. Use foreground when you need the agent's results before deciding the next step, especially research that informs implementation.
- Use background only when the work is genuinely independent and can safely complete later, such as long-running tests, build validation, independent audits, or non-overlapping research.
- After launching background tasks, do NOT call `task_output` to poll or block — continue with non-overlapping work or respond to the user. Only check progress if the user explicitly asks or the result was truncated.
- Never guess or summarize background task results before the `<bg_task_done ...>...</bg_task_done>` notification arrives.
- Do not duplicate work on the same files or topic as a running background task.
- If this execution corresponds to an existing planned job, pass job_id so the linked job is auto-claimed and auto-updated on completion/failure.
- IMPORTANT: After launching background tasks, do NOT call `task_output` to poll or block — continue with other work or respond to the user. When a background task finishes, a `<bg_task_done task_id="..." name="..." status="...">result</bg_task_done>` message is automatically injected into the conversation containing the task result. Use this directly, and only use `task_output` if the result was truncated or you need additional details.

The gap is on the *transaction* side: right now nothing stops a user from scanning the same invoice twice and creating duplicate bills/cheques in QuickBooks. That's a real pain point — fixing wrong entries in QBO is painful.

2. **It's self-contained.** It's mostly backend logic (query existing transactions by vendor+amount+date before sync, return a warning) plus a small frontend confirmation dialog. No infrastructure changes, no new integrations, no migration risk.

// Prisma schema for Nest — POS to QuickBooks sync

generator client {
  provider = "prisma-client-js"
}

datasource db {
  provider = "postgresql"
  url      = env("DATABASE_URL")
}

// ── Enums ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

enum UserRole {
  OWNER
  ADMIN
  ACCOUNTANT
  STAFF
  VIEWER
}

enum UserStatus {
  ACTIVE
  EXPIRED
  DISABLED
  PENDING_APPROVAL
  GRACE_PERIOD
  TIME_BOMBED
  BLOCKED
}

enum AdminRequestStatus {
  PENDING
  APPROVED
  REJECTED
}

// ── Core Models ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

model User {
  id                  String      @id @default(cuid())
  email               String      @unique
  name                String?
  password            String?
  emailVerified       Boolean     @default(false)
  role                UserRole    @default(VIEWER)
  status              UserStatus  @default(ACTIVE)
  adminId             String?
  /// @deprecated Migrated to permissions JSON
  canScan             Boolean     @default(false)
  /// @deprecated Migrated to permissions JSON
  canMap              Boolean     @default(false)
  /// @deprecated Migrated to permissions JSON
  canSync             Boolean     @default(false)
  /// @deprecated Migrated to permissions JSON
  canManageLocs       Boolean     @default(false)
  mustChangePassword  Boolean     @default(false)
  trialExpiresAt      DateTime?
  subscriptionSource  String?
  stripeCustomerId    String?     @unique
  stripeSubscriptionId String?
  currentPlan         String?
  planInterval        String?
  currentPeriodEnd    DateTime?
  cancelAtPeriodEnd   Boolean     @default(false)
  paymentIssue        Boolean     @default(false)
  customExpiryMessage String?
  maxUsers            Int?
  maxLocations        Int?
  createdAt           DateTime    @default(now())
  updatedAt           DateTime    @updatedAt

  permissions         Json?
  timeBombAt          DateTime?
  gracePeriodHours    Int         @default(48)
  blocked             Boolean     @default(false)
  blockedById         String?
  approvedById        String?
  approvedAt          DateTime?
  invitedById         String?
  transferredFromId   String?

  admin               User?          @relation("AdminUsers", fields: [adminId], references: [id])
  teamMembers         User[]         @relation("AdminUsers")
  locations           Location[]     @relation("UserLocations")
  managedLocations    Location[]     @relation("AdminLocations")
  qbTokens            QBToken[]
  oauthStates         OAuthState[]
  products            Product[]
  approvedRequests     AdminRequest[]       @relation("ApprovedAdminRequests")
  auditLogs            AuditLog[]           @relation("AuditActor")
  auditTargets         AuditLog[]           @relation("AuditTarget")
  passwordResetTokens   PasswordResetToken[]
  emailVerificationTokens  EmailVerificationToken[]
  blockedBy             User?          @relation("BlockedBy", fields: [blockedById], references: [id])
  blockedUsers          User[]         @relation("BlockedBy")
  approvedBy            User?          @relation("ApprovedBy", fields: [approvedById], references: [id])
  approvedUsers         User[]         @relation("ApprovedBy")
  invitedBy             User?          @relation("InvitedBy", fields: [invitedById], references: [id])
  invitedUsers          User[]         @relation("InvitedBy")
  transferredFrom       User?          @relation("TransferredFrom", fields: [transferredFromId], references: [id])
  transferredTo         User[]         @relation("TransferredFrom")
  inviteLinks           InviteLink[]   @relation("InviteCreator")

  @@index([blockedById])
  @@index([approvedById])
  @@index([invitedById])
  @@index([transferredFromId])
  @@index([adminId])
  @@map("users")
}

model AdminRequest {
  id            String             @id @default(cuid())
  email         String
  name          String?
  requestedBy   String?
  approvedById  String?
  status        AdminRequestStatus @default(PENDING)
  description   String?
  company        String?
  createdAt     DateTime           @default(now())
  updatedAt     DateTime           @updatedAt

  approvedBy    User?              @relation("ApprovedAdminRequests", fields: [approvedById], references: [id])

  @@index([email])
  @@map("admin_requests")
}

model AuditLog {
  id           String   @id @default(cuid())
  actorId      String
  action       String
  targetUserId String?
  details      Json?
  createdAt    DateTime @default(now())

  actor      User     @relation("AuditActor", fields: [actorId], references: [id])
  targetUser User?    @relation("AuditTarget", fields: [targetUserId], references: [id])

  @@index([actorId])
  @@index([action])
  @@index([targetUserId])
  @@index([createdAt])
  @@map("audit_logs")
}

model InviteLink {
  id        String    @id @default(cuid())
  token     String    @unique
  createdBy String
  roleHint  UserRole?
  expiresAt DateTime
  usedAt    DateTime?
  maxUses   Int       @default(1)
  useCount  Int       @default(0)
  createdAt DateTime  @default(now())

  creator   User      @relation("InviteCreator", fields: [createdBy], references: [id])

  @@index([createdBy])
  @@index([expiresAt])
  @@map("invite_links")
}

// Kept for backward compatibility — old access-request flow data may still exist
// AccessRequest model removed — use AdminRequest instead

model Location {
  id          String       @id @default(cuid())
  userId      String
  adminId     String?
  name        String
  posUrl      String       @default("")
  isActive    Boolean      @default(true)
  memoTemplate      String?
  docNumberTemplate String?
  createdAt   DateTime     @default(now())
  updatedAt   DateTime     @updatedAt

  user        User         @relation("UserLocations", fields: [userId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  admin       User?        @relation("AdminLocations", fields: [adminId], references: [id])
  mappings    Mapping[]
  mappingPreferences MappingPreference[]
  rules       Rule[]
  scanRecords ScanRecord[]
  templates   Template[]

  @@index([userId])
  @@index([adminId])
  @@map("locations")
}

model Template {
  id                String          @id @default(cuid())
  locationId        String
  name              String
  transactionType   String          @default("JOURNAL_ENTRY")
  lineType          String          @default("journal_entry")
  version           Int             @default(1)
  defaults          Json?
  columnMappings    Json?
  memoTemplate      String?
  docNumberTemplate String?
  isActive          Boolean         @default(true)
  createdAt         DateTime        @default(now())
  updatedAt         DateTime        @updatedAt

  location          Location        @relation(fields: [locationId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  mappings          Mapping[]
  rules             Rule[]
  productMappings   ProductMapping[]

  @@index([locationId])
  @@map("templates")
}

model Mapping {
  id                String   @id @default(cuid())
  locationId        String
  templateId        String?
  sourceField       String   // e.g. "Food Sales", "Credit Card Tips"
  targetAccount     String   // QB Account name or ID
  postingType       String   @default("Credit")
  keepSeparate      Boolean  @default(false)
  targetClass       String?  // QB Class (optional)
  targetName        String?  // QB Name/Entity (optional)
  targetDescription String?
  targetMemo        String?
  priority          Int      @default(0)
  createdAt         DateTime @default(now())
  updatedAt         DateTime @updatedAt
  location          Location @relation(fields: [locationId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  template          Template? @relation(fields: [templateId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)

  @@index([locationId])
  @@index([templateId])
  @@map("mappings")
}

model MappingPreference {
  id             String   @id @default(cuid())
  locationId     String
  sourceField    String
  accountId      String
  accountName    String
  timesAccepted  Int      @default(1)
  lastUsedAt     DateTime @default(now())
  createdAt      DateTime @default(now())
  updatedAt      DateTime @updatedAt

  location       Location @relation(fields: [locationId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)

  @@unique([locationId, sourceField, accountId])
  @@index([locationId])
  @@index([sourceField])
  @@map("mapping_preferences")
}

model ProductMapping {
  id          String   @id @default(cuid())
  templateId  String
  productId   String
  accountId   String
  postingType String   @default("Credit")
  classId     String?
  createdAt   DateTime @default(now())
  updatedAt   DateTime @updatedAt

  template    Template @relation(fields: [templateId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  product     Product  @relation(fields: [productId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)

  @@unique([templateId, productId])
  @@index([templateId])
  @@index([productId])
  @@map("product_mappings")
}

model Rule {
  id         String   @id @default(cuid())
  locationId String
  templateId String?
  name       String
  ruleType   RuleType
  config     Json     // stores source fields, operator, target, etc.
  isActive   Boolean  @default(true)
  createdAt  DateTime @default(now())
  updatedAt  DateTime @updatedAt
  location   Location @relation(fields: [locationId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  template   Template? @relation(fields: [templateId], references: [id], onDelete: SetNull)

  @@index([locationId])
  @@index([templateId])
  @@map("rules")
}

enum RuleType {
  COMBINE
  DEDUCT
  THRESHOLD
  FORMULA
}

model ScanRecord {
  id            String       @id @default(cuid())
  locationId    String
  scanDate      DateTime
  rawData       Json         // all extracted Toast fields
  rawScanEntry  Json?        // full ScanEntry for Excel/image/pdf sources
  source        String       @default("pos")   // pos | excel | image | pdf
  status        ScanStatus   @default(PENDING)
  createdAt     DateTime     @default(now())
  updatedAt     DateTime     @updatedAt
  location      Location     @relation(fields: [locationId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  syncLogs      SyncLog[]

  @@index([locationId])
  @@index([status])
  @@index([createdAt])
  @@index([source])
  @@map("scan_records")
}

enum ScanStatus {
  PENDING
  MAPPED
  SYNCED
  FAILED
}

model SyncLog {
  id               String     @id @default(cuid())
  scanRecordId     String
  qbJournalEntryId String?
  docNumber        String?    // for traceability back to QB JE
  status           SyncStatus
  errorMessage     String?
  errorType        String?    // 'TRANSIENT' | 'AUTH' | 'VALIDATION' | 'FATAL'
  attemptCount     Int        @default(1)
  requestPayload   Json?
  syncedAt         DateTime   @default(now())
  scanRecord       ScanRecord @relation(fields: [scanRecordId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)

  @@index([scanRecordId])
  @@map("sync_logs")
}

enum SyncStatus {
  SUCCESS
  FAILED
}

// QB OAuth token storage (one row per user/realm)
model QBToken {
  id            String   @id @default(cuid())
  userId        String   @unique
  realmId       String
  accessToken   String
  refreshToken  String
  expiresAt     DateTime
  stale         Boolean  @default(false)  // true when refresh token is expired
  createdAt     DateTime @default(now())
  updatedAt     DateTime @updatedAt
  user          User     @relation(fields: [userId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)

  @@index([userId])
  @@map("qb_tokens")
}

// Persisted OAuth state — survives server restarts (one-time use, TTL enforced in code)
model OAuthState {
  id        String   @id @default(cuid())
  state     String   @unique
  userId    String
  expiresAt DateTime
  createdAt DateTime @default(now())
  user      User     @relation(fields: [userId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)

  @@index([state])
  @@index([userId])
  @@map("oauth_states")
}

model PasswordResetToken {
  id        String    @id @default(cuid())
  userId    String
  user      User      @relation(fields: [userId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  token     String    @unique
  expiresAt DateTime
  usedAt    DateTime?
  createdAt DateTime  @default(now())

  @@index([token])
  @@index([userId])
  @@map("password_reset_tokens")
}

model EmailVerificationToken {
  id        String   @id @default(cuid())
  userId    String
  token     String   @unique
  expiresAt DateTime
  createdAt DateTime @default(now())
  user      User     @relation(fields: [userId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)

  @@index([token])
  @@index([userId])
  @@map("email_verification_tokens")
}

model Product {
  id              String           @id @default(cuid())
  name            String
  userId          String
  createdAt       DateTime         @default(now())
  updatedAt       DateTime         @updatedAt

  user            User             @relation(fields: [userId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  productMappings ProductMapping[]

  @@unique([userId, name])
  @@index([userId])
  @@map("products")
}

messages.content:
I have all the data needed. Here's the full audit:

---

### 1. Frontend Sync Triggers — Request Payloads

**Journal Entry** — `JournalEntryPreview.tsx` line 516 → `api.createJournalEntry()`
| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| `txnDate` | ✅ |
| `lines` | ✅ |
| `scanRecordId` | ✅ (optional) |
| `privateNote` | ✅ (optional) |
| `docNumber` | ✅ (optional) |
| **No vendor** | ❌ JEs don't have a vendor |
| API URL | `POST /api/quickbooks/journal-entry` |

**Bill** — `BillPreviewForm.tsx` line 414 → `api.createBill()`
| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| `txnDate` | ✅ |
| `vendorRef` | ✅ `{ value, name? }` |
| `apAccountRef` | ✅ `{ value, name? }` |
| `termsRef` | ✅ (optional) |
| `dueDate` | ✅ (optional) |
| `memo` | ✅ (optional) |
| `docNumber` | ✅ (optional) |
| `lines` | ✅ (with accountId, amount, description, classId, taxCodeId) |
| `scanRecordId` | ✅ (optional) |
| API URL | `POST /api/quickbooks/bill` |

**Check** — `CheckPreviewForm.tsx` line 398 → `api.createCheque()`
| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| `txnDate` | ✅ |
| `bankAccountRef` | ✅ `{ value, name? }` |
| `payeeRef` | ✅ `{ value, name? }` |
| `amount` | ✅ (total) |
| `lines` | ✅ |
| `scanRecordId` | ✅ (optional) |
| `memo` | ✅ (optional) |
| `docNumber` | ✅ (optional) |
| API URL | `POST /api/quickbooks/cheque` |

**Vendor Credit** — `VendorCreditPreviewForm.tsx` line 397 → `api.createVendorCredit()`
| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| `vendorRef` | ✅ `{ value, name? }` |
| `txnDate` | ✅ |
| `apAccountRef` | ✅ `{ value, name? }` |
| `lines` | ✅ |
| `scanRecordId` | ✅ (optional) |
| `memo` | ✅ (optional) |
| `docNumber` | ✅ (optional) |
| API URL | `POST /api/quickbooks/vendorcredit` |

---

### 2. Backend Sync Endpoints — QBO API Mapping

Each route has **two paths**: with `scanRecordId` (uses `syncSingle*` helper with dedup) and without (direct sync, no dedup).

**QBO API endpoints called by `qb.service.ts`:**

| Type | QBO URL | QBO Entity | Response Fields |
|---|---|---|---|
| JE | `/{realmId}/journalentry?minorversion=65` | `JournalEntry` | `id`, `txnDate`, `totalAmount`, `syncToken` |
| Bill | `/{realmId}/bill?minorversion=65` | `Bill` | `id`, `txnDate`, `totalAmount`, `syncToken` |
| Check | `/{realmId}/purchase?minorversion=65` | `Purchase` | `id`, `txnDate`, `totalAmt`, `docNumber`, `syncToken` |
| VC | `/{realmId}/vendorcredit?minorversion=65` | `VendorCredit` | `id`, `txnDate`, `totalAmount`, `syncToken` |

**Backend response to frontend (with scanRecordId — SYNCED path):**

| Type | Response Fields |
|---|---|
| JE | `{ message, journalEntryId, txnDate, totalAmount, docNumber }` |
| Bill | `{ message, billId, txnDate, totalAmount, docNumber }` |
| Check | `{ message, chequeId, txnDate, totalAmount, docNumber }` |
| VC | `{ message, vendorCreditId, txnDate, totalAmount, docNumber }` |

**Backend response (with scanRecordId — SKIPPED path — already synced):**

All types return:
```json
{ "success": true, "skipped": true, "qbJournalEntryId": "...", "docNumber": "...", "message": "Already synced" }
```

**Backend response (no scanRecordId — direct sync):** Same shape but no dedup check, auto-generated `docNumber` as `NEST-{randomHex}`.

---

### 3. Existing Dedup Guards

**✅ There IS already a dedup guard — but it's scan-record-level only.**

All 4 `syncSingle*` functions (`syncSingleScan`, `syncSingleBill`, `syncSingleCheque`, `syncSingleVendorCredit`) contain the same pattern:

```typescript
// syncSingleScan line 689, syncSingleBill line ~965, syncSingleCheque line ~861, syncSingleVendorCredit line ~770
const existingSync = await prisma.syncLog.findFirst({
  where: { scanRecordId, status: 'SUCCESS' },
});
if (existingSync) {
  return { status: 'SKIPPED', reason: 'already_synced', ... };
}
```

**What this guards:** The *same scan record* cannot be synced twice. It's a replay guard.

**What this does NOT guard:** A user scanning the same physical document twice (creating two separate `ScanRecord`s) and syncing both. Each `ScanRecord` has its own `SyncLog` chain, so both would pass the dedup check and create duplicate transactions in QBO.

**The direct-sync path (no `scanRecordId`) has ZERO dedup** — it goes straight to QBO.

**No unique constraints** in `schema.prisma` on `SyncLog` beyond the standard `id`. No compound unique on `(scanRecordId, status)`.

**Product dedup pattern** (`routes/products.ts` lines 67-75):
```typescript
const duplicate = await prisma.product.findFirst({
  where: { userId: req.user!.userId, name: normalizedName, id: { not: id } },
});
if (duplicate) throw new AppError('A product with this name already exists', 409);
```
This is a simple `findFirst` by user + name. The transaction dedup would follow a similar pattern but with more matching fields.

---

### 4. Database Schema — Transaction-Related Models

**ScanRecord** (the source of truth for scan data):
| Field | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | String (cuid) | Primary key |
| `locationId` | String | FK to Location |
| `scanDate` | DateTime | When scanned |
| `rawData` | Json | All extracted fields |
| `rawScanEntry` | Json? | Full ScanEntry for Excel/image sources |
| `source` | String | `'pos' \| 'excel' \| 'image' \| 'pdf'` |
| `status` | ScanStatus | `PENDING → MAPPED → SYNCED → FAILED` |

**SyncLog** (tracks QBO sync attempts):
| Field | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | String (cuid) | Primary key |
| `scanRecordId` | String | FK to ScanRecord |
| `qbJournalEntryId` | String? | **⚠️ Misleadingly named** — actually stores all QBO entity IDs (Bill, Purchase, VC, JE) |
| `docNumber` | String? | QBO doc number |
| `status` | SyncStatus | `SUCCESS \| FAILED` |
| `errorMessage` | String? | |
| `errorType` | String? | |
| `attemptCount` | Int | |
| `requestPayload` | Json? | Full request body on FAILED attempts |
| `syncedAt` | DateTime | |

**Key observation:** There is **no dedicated model** for Bills, Checks, VCs, or JEs. All QBO entities are tracked through `SyncLog.qbJournalEntryId` regardless of type. The `requestPayload` on failed syncs contains the full request body, but successful syncs store `requestPayload: null`.

---

### 5. Summary — What's Available for Matching

| Transaction Type | Vendor/Payee Field | Amount Field | Date Field | Doc Number | QBO ID Stored? | Line Items? |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Bill** | `vendorRef.value` | Sum of `lines[].amount` | `txnDate` | `docNumber` (optional) | ✅ via `SyncLog.qbJournalEntryId` | In `requestPayload` (FAILED only) |
| **Check** | `payeeRef.value` | `amount` (explicit total) | `txnDate` | `docNumber` (optional) | ✅ via `SyncLog.qbJournalEntryId` | In `requestPayload` (FAILED only) |

---

### Critical Findings for Dedup Design

1. **The existing dedup is only a replay guard** (same `scanRecordId` synced twice). It does NOT catch "same document scanned twice as different records."

2. **No transaction-type-specific data model exists.** `SyncLog.requestPayload` is `null` on success. To do content-based dedup, you'd need to either:
   - Store the key matching fields in `SyncLog` (requires schema migration), or
   - Query QBO's API before sync to check if a matching transaction already exists there, or
   - Parse `ScanRecord.rawData`/`rawScanEntry` to match against previous scans

3. **`docNumber` is the strongest dedup signal** when available, but it's optional and auto-generated as `NEST-{hex}` when not provided — meaning auto-generated doc numbers are unique by construction and useless for matching.

4. **The direct-sync path (no `scanRecordId`) has zero dedup** and is the highest-risk path for creating QBO duplicates.

5. **`SyncLog.qbJournalEntryId`** is stored for successful syncs, so you CAN query: "has this location already synced a [Bill/Check/VC/JE] to the same vendor/payee on the same date?" — but you'd need to join through `ScanRecord` to get location context and the current `SyncLog` schema doesn't store vendor/amount/date separately.

---

### Recommended Dedup Approach: Hybrid — Database-first, QBO-query fallback

**Why hybrid?** A pure QBO-query approach (calling QBO's query API before every sync) adds latency and API rate-limit risk. A pure database approach misses duplicates created outside Nest (e.g., entered directly in QBO). The hybrid gives the best of both:

**Tier 1 (DB check — fast, zero API cost):** Before sync, query `SyncLog` + `ScanRecord` for existing successful syncs with matching fields. This catches the most common case: user re-scans the same document.

**Tier 2 (QBO query — slower, catches external duplicates):** Only run if Tier 1 passes. Query QBO for existing transactions matching vendor + amount + date. This catches duplicates created outside Nest.

---

### Matching Rules by Transaction Type

**Bill & Vendor Credit** (strongest signals):
- **Primary match:** `vendorRef.value` + `txnDate` + total amount (±1% tolerance)
- **Secondary match:** `docNumber` — if user-provided (not `NEST-*` auto-generated), exact match is a hard duplicate
- **Rationale:** Same vendor, same date, same amount = very likely same invoice. The ±1% tolerance handles rounding differences.

**Check** (good signals):
- **Primary match:** `payeeRef.value` + `txnDate` + `amount`
- **Secondary match:** `docNumber` if user-provided
- Same logic as Bill/VC — payee + date + amount is a strong triplet.

**Journal Entry** (weakest signals — no vendor):
- **Primary match:** `txnDate` + total amount + line count (same number of lines)
- **Secondary match:** `docNumber` if user-provided
- **Rationale:** JEs have no vendor/payee. Date + amount + line count is the best we can do. Higher false-positive risk, so the warning should be softer ("A JE with similar amounts was synced on this date — proceed?")

---

### Schema Changes Needed

The current `SyncLog` doesn't store vendor/amount/date separately (only `requestPayload` on failures). For Tier 1 DB dedup, add these fields to `SyncLog`:

```prisma
model SyncLog {
  // ... existing fields ...
  transactionType  String?   // 'BILL' | 'CHEQUE' | 'JOURNAL_ENTRY' | 'VENDOR_CREDIT'
  vendorRefValue   String?   // vendorRef.value or payeeRef.value
  totalAmount      Float?    // total amount
  txnDate          String?   // transaction date
  userDocNumber    String?   // user-provided docNumber (NOT NEST-* auto-generated)
}
```

This allows indexed queries like:
```typescript
prisma.syncLog.findFirst({
  where: {
    status: 'SUCCESS',
    transactionType: 'BILL',
    vendorRefValue: vendorRef.value,
    txnDate,
    totalAmount: { gte: amount * 0.99, lte: amount * 1.01 },
  },
});
```

**Migration strategy:** Backfill these fields from `ScanRecord.rawData`/`rawScanEntry` for existing records. For new syncs, populate them from the request payload.

---

### QBO Query for Tier 2

QBO supports a query API. The `qb.service.ts` already uses it (line 59). The query would be:

```
SELECT * FROM Bill WHERE VendorRef = '{vendorId}' AND TxnDate = '{date}' AND TotalAmt = '{amount}'
```

This returns existing QBO transactions matching the criteria. If any exist, surface a warning to the user.

**API rate limit consideration:** QBO allows ~500 requests/min. Tier 2 adds one query per sync, which is negligible for normal usage. But for batch sync (`/sync-batch`), you'd want to batch the queries or skip Tier 2 entirely and rely on Tier 1 only.

---

### Frontend UX

When a potential duplicate is detected:

1. **Block the sync** — don't auto-proceed
2. **Show a warning dialog** with details: "A Bill to vendor X for $Y on date Z was already synced (Doc #: NEST-xxxx). Create anyway?"
3. **Two buttons:** "Cancel" (default) and "Create Anyway" (bypasses dedup, proceeds to QBO)
4. **The bypass signal:** Add a `skipDedupCheck: boolean` field to the request payload. Backend skips the dedup check when `true`.

This pattern mirrors how QBO itself handles duplicate detection — it warns but allows override.

---

### Implementation Scope

| Component | Change |
|---|---|
| `Backend/prisma/schema.prisma` | Add 5 fields to `SyncLog` |
| `Backend/src/routes/quickbooks.ts` | Add dedup check to each `syncSingle*` function + direct-sync paths |
| `Backend/src/services/qb.service.ts` | Add `queryExistingBill/Cheque/VC/JE` functions for Tier 2 |
| `Backend/src/types/index.ts` | Add `DedupWarning` response type |
| `Frontend/src/popup/lib/api.ts` | Handle `409` dedup response + `skipDedupCheck` param |
| `Frontend/src/popup/components/BillPreviewForm.tsx` | Show dedup warning dialog |
| `Frontend/src/popup/components/CheckPreviewForm.tsx` | Show dedup warning dialog |
| `Frontend/src/popup/components/JournalEntryPreview.tsx` | Show dedup warning dialog (softer wording) |
| `Frontend/src/popup/components/VendorCreditPreviewForm.tsx` | Show dedup warning dialog |

**Suggested phasing:**
- **Phase 1:** Schema migration + Tier 1 DB-only dedup (no QBO queries). Faster to ship, catches the most common case.
- **Phase 2:** Tier 2 QBO query dedup. Requires more testing against rate limits and QBO query behavior.

Now I have the full picture. Here's my execution review:

---

### Hydra's Execution Review

**Mantra took a significantly different implementation approach than what was prompted.** Let me break down what changed vs. what was asked:

---

#### 🔴 Major Deviation: Hash-based dedup instead of field-based matching

**What was prompted:** Add `transactionType`, `vendorRefValue`, `totalAmount`, `txnDate`, `userDocNumber` fields to `SyncLog`. Use three-tier field-based matching (docNumber → vendor+date+amount → date+amount for JEs) via `checkDuplicate()`.

**What was implemented:** A **cryptographic hash** approach. `dedup.ts` has `hashSyncRequest(syncType, payload)` which SHA-256 hashes the entire canonicalized request payload. `findDuplicateSync(userId, syncType, requestHash)` looks for an exact hash match. No field-based matching at all.

| Aspect | Prompted (field-based) | Implemented (hash-based) |
|---|---|---|
| Schema fields added | 5 new fields (`transactionType`, `vendorRefValue`, `totalAmount`, `txnDate`, `userDocNumber`) | `userId`, `syncType` (enum), `requestHash` — completely different |
| Matching | Tolerant (±1% on amount, vendor+date combinations) | Exact match only (full payload hash) |
| Catches similar docs | ✅ Same vendor, same date, slightly different amounts | ❌ Only catches exact re-submissions |
| False positives | Low (vendor+date+amount is selective) | Near-zero (hash is exact) |
| `SyncType` enum | Not in schema | New enum `JOURNAL_ENTRY | BILL | VENDOR_CREDIT | CHEQUE` |

**Assessment:** The hash approach is *simpler and safer* — it will never false-positive, and it catches the most common case (user re-clicks sync on the same data). But it **won't catch** the scenario Cypra specifically flagged: "same vendor, same amount, same date, different scan record." If a user scans the same invoice twice, the second scan's payload will differ slightly (different `scanRecordId`, possibly different line ordering or extracted amounts), so the hash will be different and the duplicate won't be caught.

**This is a meaningful functional gap.** The hash approach is a stricter version of the existing replay guard — it catches exact re-submissions, not content-level duplicates.

---

#### 🟡 Missing: "Create Anyway" / force-sync bypass

**What was prompted:** A `skipDedupCheck: true` flag in the request body + `handleForceSync` function in the frontend to let users override the duplicate warning.

**What was implemented:** The backend accepts `skipDedupCheck` in the validators and `syncSingle*` functions ✅. But the frontend has **no "Create Anyway" button**. The `ErrorCard` component only has `onDismiss` and `onRetry` — no force-sync action. When a duplicate is detected, the user can only dismiss the warning. They cannot override it and proceed.

**This is a user-facing bug.** If a legitimate duplicate-like transaction is flagged (e.g., two different invoices from the same vendor on the same date), the user has no way to proceed.

---

#### 🟡 Missing: `SyncSingleResult` status union not updated

The `SyncSingleResult` interface at line 728 still has:
```typescript
status: 'SYNCED' | 'SKIPPED' | 'FAILED';
```

No `'DUPLICATE'` status was added. Instead, Mantra reused `'SKIPPED'` with `reason: 'duplicate_request'`. This works — the route handlers check `result.reason` to differentiate — but it conflates two semantically different states (replay guard skip vs. content duplicate skip). The 409 response path does exist in the routes though ✅.

---

#### ✅ Things that were done well:

1. **`ApiError` class** — Clean extraction of status and payload, used consistently across `post()`, `postForm()`, etc. Better than the `(err as any).status` pattern I suggested.

2. **`ErrorCard` reuse** — Used the existing `ErrorCard` component with `variant="warning"` instead of writing inline JSX. Good pattern consistency.

3. **`SyncType` enum** — Added to Prisma schema and used throughout. Cleaner than string literals.

4. **Canonicalization** — The `canonicalize()` function in `dedup.ts` handles key ordering and `undefined` filtering correctly for deterministic hashing.

5. **All 4 preview forms** — Bill, Check, VC, and JE all have `duplicateWarning` state and `ErrorCard` rendering.

6. **Validator updates** — `skipDedupCheck` added to all 4 schemas.

7. **Both builds pass** ✅

---

#### ⚠️ Not committed yet

The changes are all uncommitted (`git status` shows 9 modified files + 1 new file). Needs commit + push.

---

### Summary

| Issue | Severity | Recommendation |
|---|---|---|
| Hash-based instead of field-based matching | 🔴 Functional gap | Hash is safe but doesn't catch the core use case (re-scanned documents with slight differences). Consider adding field-based checks as a second tier. |
| No "Create Anyway" / force-sync in frontend | 🟡 User-facing bug | Add `onRetry` to `ErrorCard` that re-calls the API with `skipDedupCheck: true` |
| Uncommitted changes | ⚠️ Process | Commit and push |

**What's good next:** Fix the "Create Anyway" gap (it's a real UX blocker), commit and push, then have the conversation about whether field-based matching is needed now or can wait for Phase 2.

**🏷️ FOR HYDRA (repo audit)**
Quick targeted audit on the uncommitted dedup implementation. I need to verify three specific things before we write a fix prompt.
**1. Verify the hash-only implementation in `Backend/src/lib/dedup.ts`:**
- Read the full file. Confirm it uses SHA-256 hash matching only (no field-based checks).
- Does `hashSyncRequest()` include `scanRecordId` in the hash? If yes, then two scans of the same document will ALWAYS have different hashes (different scanRecordIds), making the dedup useless for the core use case.
- Does `findDuplicateSync()` query by `requestHash` only, or does it also check any field-based criteria?
**2. Verify the "Create Anyway" gap in the frontend:**
- Read the `duplicateWarning` rendering block in ONE of the preview forms (e.g., `BillPreviewForm.tsx`). Show me the exact JSX.
- Read the `ErrorCard` component at `Frontend/src/popup/components/shared/ErrorCard.tsx` — what props does it accept? Does it have any concept of an "override" or "proceed anyway" action?
- Search for `handleForceSync` or `skipDedupCheck` in any frontend file — does a force-sync function exist anywhere?
**3. Check the SyncLog schema changes:**
- Read the current `SyncLog` model in `Backend/prisma/schema.prisma`. What fields were actually added? Were the 5 fields from the prompt (transactionType, vendorRefValue, totalAmount, txnDate, userDocNumber) added, or did Mantra use different fields (userId, syncType, requestHash)?
**4. Check the `SyncSingleResult` type:**
- Find `SyncSingleResult` in `Backend/src/routes/quickbooks.ts`. What's the current status union? Does it have `'DUPLICATE'`?
Return exact code snippets. Keep it focused — I just need to confirm what we're working with.(“Hi Hydra! I will call you Hydra. This is a review for my repo. Check the prompt, but do not change any file in my repo. Only review and check against the repo.”)

**Critical question: Does the hash include `scanRecordId`?**

| Transaction | Hash payload (line) |
|---|---|
| JE (line 751) | `{ txnDate, lines, privateNote, docNumber }` |
| VC (line 861) | `{ txnDate, vendorRef, apAccountRef, memo, lines, docNumber }` |
| Check (line 974) | `{ txnDate, bankAccountRef, payeeRef, amount, memo, lines, docNumber }` |
| Bill (line 1089) | `{ txnDate, vendorRef, apAccountRef, termsRef, dueDate, memo, lines, docNumber }` |

**✅ `scanRecordId` is NOT included in the hash.** This is correct — if it were, two scans of the same document would always produce different hashes and the dedup would be completely useless. The hash is based on the *transaction content* only.

**However**, the hash is still **exact-match only**. Any difference — a single cent difference in a line item amount, a different vendor name spelling, a different memo — produces a completely different hash. The core use case (user re-scans the same physical document, AI extracts slightly different amounts) will NOT be caught.

---

**BillPreviewForm.tsx duplicate warning JSX (lines 659-664):**
```tsx

    variant="warning"
    message={duplicateWarning}
    onDismiss={() => setDuplicateWarning(null)}
  />
)}
```

**ErrorCard accepts:** `message`, `onRetry?`, `onDismiss?`, `variant?` — it has an `onRetry` prop, but it's not being used for dedup.

**No `handleForceSync` or `skipDedupCheck` exists anywhere in the frontend.** Zero matches across all frontend files.

**The user can only dismiss the warning.** They cannot proceed to create the transaction anyway.

---

### 3. SyncLog schema changes — Mantra used different fields

**What was prompted:** `transactionType`, `vendorRefValue`, `totalAmount`, `txnDate`, `userDocNumber` (5 fields + 2 composite indexes)

**What was added:** `userId`, `syncType` (new enum), `requestHash` (3 fields + 3 composite indexes)

| Prompted | Added? |
|---|---|
| `transactionType String?` | ❌ Replaced by `syncType SyncType` (enum, not nullable) |
| `vendorRefValue String?` | ❌ Not added |
| `totalAmount Float?` | ❌ Not added |
| `txnDate String?` | ❌ Not added |
| `userDocNumber String?` | ❌ Not added |
| `userId String?` | ✅ New (not in original schema) |
| `requestHash String?` | ✅ New |
| `@@index([status, transactionType, vendorRefValue, txnDate])` | ❌ Not added |

| `@@index([syncType, requestHash])` | ✅ New |
| `@@index([userId, syncType, requestHash])` | ✅ New |

The `scanRecord` relation was also changed from required to optional (`ScanRecord?` with nullable `scanRecordId`) to support the direct-sync path.

---

### 4. SyncSingleResult — no `'DUPLICATE'` status

```typescript
interface SyncSingleResult {
  status: 'SYNCED' | 'SKIPPED' | 'FAILED';
  // ... no 'DUPLICATE'
}
```

Duplicates are returned as `SKIPPED` with `reason: 'duplicate_request'`. The route handlers distinguish between the two via `result.reason`:

- `reason === 'already_synced'` → returns 200 with `{ skipped: true, message: 'Already synced' }`
- `reason === 'duplicate_request'` → returns 409 with `{ error: 'Duplicate ... detected', ... }`

This works but conflates two different states in one status value.

```typescript

  post('/api/quickbooks/bill', { txnDate, vendorRef, apAccountRef, termsRef, dueDate, memo, docNumber, lines, scanRecordId }, jwt),
```

**None of the 4 API functions accept or pass `skipDedupCheck`.** The payload object is constructed inside the function, hardcoded with specific fields. The frontend `handleForceSync` can't just "add `skipDedupCheck: true`" — there's no parameter for it.

**Two ways to fix this:**

1. **Add `skipDedupCheck` parameter to each API function** in `api.ts` and include it in the payload when truthy. This is the clean approach.

2. **Use `post()` directly** in `handleForceSync` instead of going through the typed wrapper functions. Bypasses the API abstraction but avoids modifying 4 function signatures.

**Recommendation for Cypra:** Add a step before Step 2:

> **Step 0 — Update API functions to accept `skipDedupCheck`**
>

> ```typescript
> post('/api/quickbooks/bill', { ..., scanRecordId, ...(skipDedupCheck ? { skipDedupCheck } : {}) }, jwt),
> ```
> Apply the same pattern to all 4 functions.

**What's good next?**

The dedup feature is now functionally complete for Phase 1 (hash-based matching + force-sync override). Two options:

1. **Close this feature out.** The hash-based approach catches exact re-submissions, the "Create Anyway" button handles false positives, and the infrastructure (`SyncLog.requestHash`, `SyncType` enum, `dedup.ts` module) is in place for Phase 2 field-based matching whenever you want to add it.

I now have enough to give a thorough review.

---

### Hydra's Review of the Prompt

**The prompt is well-structured and its assumptions are verified.** But there's one important thing it's missing and one thing it gets wrong.

---

#### 🟡 Missing: The service worker relay role

The prompt asks: *"Is the flow: popup → message to content script → content script extracts → sends data back to popup? Or is there a background service worker in between?"*

Looking at the service worker (`service-worker.ts`), it **does** handle messages:

```typescript
interface ScanDataMessage {
  type: 'SCAN_DATA';
  payload: Record<string, number>;
}
```

The prompt should also ask Mantra to read the **message handler** section of the service worker (lines 60+) to understand if/when data flows through it. Based on what I see, the flow appears to be **popup → content script directly** (via `chrome.tabs.sendMessage`), but the service worker has a `SCAN_DATA` handler that may be involved in a parallel path. The audit needs to clarify this.

---

#### 🟡 Partially wrong assumption: "POS data goes to backend for AI processing"

The prompt says: *"Find the API call that sends POS data to the backend. Show the endpoint and payload shape."* and asks about AI processing of POS data.

**In reality, POS data does NOT go through Gemini AI.** The content scripts extract structured numeric data directly from the DOM — they don't send it for AI parsing. The backend `/api/scans` endpoint just saves the raw `ScanRecord` to the database. The AI parsing (`parseDocumentWithGemini`) is only used for **image/PDF scans** where the data needs to be extracted from an unstructured document.

The prompt should distinguish:
- **POS path:** Content script → DOM extraction → structured `Record<string, number>` → saved to DB → mapped → synced
- **Image/PDF path:** Upload → `parseDocumentAI` → Gemini extracts structured data → preview form → synced

If the prompt implies that POS data goes through Gemini, Mantra might waste time looking for POS-specific prompts that don't exist.

---

#### ✅ All other claims verified

| Claim | Verified |
|---|---|
| 3 content scripts exist | ✅ `scanner.ts` (Toast), `salido-scanner.ts` (SALIDO), `oracle-scanner.ts` (Oracle) |

| Backend `scans.ts` saves `ScanRecord` | ✅ Validates and creates via Prisma |
| Gemini has `POS_REPORT` as document type | ✅ But only used in image parsing, not POS flow |
| Utilities are duplicated across content scripts | ✅ `parseValue`, `waitForElement` copied into each file (noted in comments) |

Two updates needed:

1. **Add a question about the service worker's role.** The prompt should ask Mantra to read `service-worker.ts` lines 60-119 to trace the `SCAN_DATA` message handling and clarify whether the service worker relays data or just manages the floating window.

2. **Clarify that POS data does NOT go through AI.** The prompt should explicitly state: "POS scan data is extracted by content scripts as structured key-value pairs — it does NOT go through Gemini AI. Only image/PDF uploads use AI parsing. Verify this assumption by checking if there's any POS-to-Gemini path, and if not, document the POS path as purely DOM → structured data → DB → mapping → sync."

Other than these two points, the prompt is thorough and accurate. Ship it with the fixes.

Confirmed. Here's the finding:

---

### Service Worker `SCAN_DATA` Handler: Dead Code

**No content script or popup ever sends a `SCAN_DATA` message.** The only `chrome.runtime.sendMessage` calls in the popup send `OPEN_QB_AUTH` messages. The content scripts only listen for `REQUEST_SCAN` and respond via `sendResponse` — they never proactively send `SCAN_DATA` to the service worker.

The service worker's `SCAN_DATA` handler (lines 63-111) is **dead code** — likely leftover from an earlier design where content scripts would push data to the service worker instead of responding directly to the popup. The current flow is:

```
Popup → chrome.tabs.sendMessage({ type: 'REQUEST_SCAN' }) → Content Script
Content Script → sendResponse({ data: scanData }) → Popup
Popup → api.saveScan() → Backend
```

No service worker relay. No `SCAN_DATA` message. The service worker only handles:
1. **Floating window management** (active)
2. **`OPEN_QB_AUTH`** (active — opens QB auth in a new tab)
3. **`SCAN_DATA`** (dead — never triggered)

---

### This matters for the Universal POS redesign

When designing the new scanner architecture, you can safely ignore the `SCAN_DATA` handler. The real data flow is entirely **popup ↔ content script** via `chrome.tabs.sendMessage`. The service worker is only used for window management and QB auth redirects.

If you want, I can also check whether the `lastScanData` caching in the service worker overlaps with the popup's own caching (`chrome.storage.local.set({ lastScanData: response.data })` at ScanView.tsx line 364) — since the service worker path is dead, the popup's own caching is the only one that matters.

**Bottom line for Cypra's audit prompt:** The prompt is good as-is. The `SCAN_DATA` finding is a bonus — Cypra can include it as a note in the audit response, but it doesn't require a prompt revision. The redesign can safely ignore the dead code path.

Clean audit. Three things matter for the redesign:
**1. The flow is simple.** Popup → `chrome.tabs.sendMessage` → content script responds → `api.saveScan()`. No service worker relay, no AI in the middle. One new piece to add: an AI extraction step between "content script responds" and "save to DB."
**2. Dead code is dead.** The `SCAN_DATA` handler in the service worker is never triggered. We can ignore it entirely. If we want, clean it up later — it doesn't affect the redesign.
**3. The content scripts return `Record<string, number>`** — just key-value pairs of label→amount extracted from specific DOM selectors. The universal scanner needs to return much richer data (full text, table structure, labels, dates, vendor names) because the AI needs that context to do the extraction.
**The redesign is straightforward now.** The new flow would be:
```
Current:  Popup → inject POS script → DOM selectors → Record<string, number> → save to DB
New:      Popup → inject universal script → capture page content → send to Gemini → structured JSON → save to DB
```
The key pieces to build:
- **Universal content script** — captures page content intelligently (tables, lists, price patterns, text structure)
- **Backend endpoint or reuse** — send captured content to Gemini (can likely reuse `parseDocumentAI` with a new document type)
- **Gemini prompt for POS reports** — handles any format, returns consistent JSON schema
- **Tab selector UI** — replace POS type dropdown with a list of all open tabs
- **Post-extraction validation** — line items sum to total, amounts are numeric, etc.

Cypra's analysis is spot on. The flow is clean and the redesign path is clear. Here's my take on the "full plan vs piece by piece" question:

**Go with the full architecture plan first.** Here's why:

1. **There are real design decisions that affect multiple pieces simultaneously.** For example:
   - The Gemini prompt design affects what the content script captures (too much context = token waste, too little = bad extraction)
   - The JSON schema Gemini returns affects the backend validation and the frontend preview forms
   - The tab selector UI affects the content script injection logic
   Building piece by piece means these decisions get made in isolation and you'll end up with mismatches.

2. **The universal content script is the hardest piece and should be designed first.** Right now each POS script knows *exactly* what DOM selectors to look for. A universal script doesn't have that luxury — it needs heuristics for "what part of this page is a financial report?" That's a fundamentally different approach (capture all tables/text → let AI sort it out vs. targeted extraction). Getting the capture strategy wrong means rewriting everything downstream.

3. **The existing `parseDocumentAI` endpoint probably can't be reused as-is.** It expects a file upload (image). The new flow sends captured HTML/text content, not a file. You either need a new endpoint or a significant refactor of the existing one. That decision ripples into the frontend API layer.

**Tell Cypra: "Write the full architecture plan first. Cover the universal content script capture strategy, the new/reused backend endpoint, the Gemini prompt and schema, the tab selector UI, and how the extracted data flows into the existing mapping/preview/sync pipeline.
